title: Transverse tame boundary exchange of open direct image and extension by zero
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. Fix a finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$, let $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ on profinite sets, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]; put $C_{F,T}=p_T^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories and direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-regular-scheme], let $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ be a reduced strict normal crossings divisor with finitely many components [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and put $W=Y\setminus D$. Let $L$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,W}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Assume that on every strict henselization at a geometric point, with parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ cutting out the branches of $D$, $L$ becomes constant on the inverse-limit cover of the complement obtained by adjoining compatible $n$th roots of all $t_i$ for every $n$ prime to $p$. This is the meaning of tame here; with no branches the cover is the identity. Write $L_F=C_{F,W}\otimes_{C_{E,W}}L$, an ordinary tensor, for $F=E,\Omega$.

Partition $A=A_o\sqcup A_i$, and put $V=Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\in A_o}D_a$ and $Y^\circ=Y\setminus\bigcup_{a\in A_i}D_a$. Denote the open immersions by $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $c:Y^\circ\hookrightarrow Y$, $b:W\hookrightarrow V$, and $a:W\hookrightarrow Y^\circ$; their square is cartesian. Use exact extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. For $F=E,\Omega$, let
$$e_F:c_!Ra_{*,C_F}(L_F[0])\longrightarrow Rj_{*,C_F}b_!(L_F[0])$$
be the following canonical map. Open slice restriction identifies $c^*Rj_*b_!L_F$ with $Ra_*L_F$. Its inverse is a map $Ra_*L_F\to c^*Rj_*b_!L_F$; take its adjunct under $c_!\dashv c^*$. Then $e_F$ is an isomorphism. These maps are natural in $L_F$ and commute, after restriction of scalars, with $L_E\to\operatorname{Res}L_\Omega$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, using the ordinary direct-image and extension-by-zero scalar-restriction identifications. In particular $Rj_*b_!L_F$ restricts to zero on the union of the inner components, even at intersections with outer components. This is a single-coefficient geometric exchange assertion, without any assertion that scalar extension commutes with $Rj_*$. Empty parts of the partition, the empty divisor, and rank zero are allowed.

proof.text: Fix $F=E$ or $\Omega$. Put $Z=\bigcup_{a\in A_i}D_a$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$, $h:Z\cap V\hookrightarrow V$, $K=Rb_*L_F[0]$, and $B=Rj_*b_!L_F[0]$. By [lem-sfb-open-square-closed-unit-triangle] there is a triangle $i^*B\to i^*Rj_*K\xrightarrow{i^*u_F}i^*Rj_*h_*h^*K\to$, where $u_F=Rj_*(\eta_{h,K})$. $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $0,1$), so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $Y$ locally Noetherian; finite type gives quasi-compactness, hence $Y$ is Noetherian.

proof.text: For any profinite $G_o,G_i$, use the exact inflation adjunctions of [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation]. Their composite is product inflation and its conjugate is $M^{G_o\times G_i}=(M^{G_i})^{G_o}$. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] with this identity comparison. It makes $\theta:R\Gamma_{G_o\times G_i}\to R\Gamma_{G_o}R\Gamma_{G_i}^{G_o}$ invertible, normalized on K-injectives by that same invariants identity.

proof.text: For every $S_J$ with $J\cap A_i\ne\varnothing$, [lem-sfb-partial-kummer-boundary-unit-model] identifies $u_F|_{S_J}$ on a pro-etale cover with $p_T^*\theta_{M_F}$. Regularity, strict normal crossings and the stipulated Kummer triviality are precisely its hypotheses. Step 2 makes the covered maps invertible. By [lem-zl-condensed-cover-restriction-conservative], $u_F|_{S_J}$ is invertible on the entire stratum.

proof.text: $Z$ is Noetherian (closed in the Noetherian $Y$; quotients of Noetherian rings are Noetherian). The $S_J$ with $J\cap A_i\ne\varnothing$ are locally closed, disjoint and cover $Z$ ($z$ lies only in $S_{J(z)}$, $J(z)=\{a:z\in D_a\}$), so with reduced structures they stratify $Z$. By [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], $D(Z,C_F)$ is the derived category of modules over the section-ring sheaf of $C_{F,Z}$, with the same sheaves. [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection] with identity covers and step 3 make $i^*u_F$ invertible, and the triangle of [lem-sfb-open-square-closed-unit-triangle] gives $i^*B=0$, including at intersections of inner and outer components.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent all-continuous tame-boundary obligation; assembly after the 2026-10-22 re-split

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-open-square-support-scalar-counit] to the cartesian open square and $M=L_F[0]$. Its map is the prescribed adjunct $e_F$, so $i^*B=0$ makes $e_F$ invertible. The same lemma gives naturality and, for $R=C_E$, $R'=C_\Omega$, $\mu:x\mapsto1\otimes x$, the required scalar-restriction square. These are the all-continuous rings throughout; scalar extension is never moved through $Rj_*$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent all-continuous tame-boundary obligation; assembly after the 2026-10-22 re-split

proof.text: Step 4 is the stated zero restriction on the union of inner components, including its intersections with outer components. If $A_i=\varnothing$, then $c,b$ are identities and $e_F$ is the identity under the canonical comparisons; if $A_o=\varnothing$, $j,a$ are identities and the map is again the identity on extension by zero. For $D=\varnothing$ both checks coincide. For rank zero all objects and maps are zero. These cases also follow from the same proof (there are no boundary strata when $Z=\varnothing$).
